newsitem.title: UK: Pearson comprises three core divisions.
newsitem.headline: Pearson comprises three core divisions.

text.p: British media and leisure company Pearson, at the centre of recent bid speculation, divides its activities into three core divisions - Information, Education and Entertainment.
The following table gives latest full-year (1995) figures for each division and lists their most important components:
INFORMATION :
Sales 759.1 million stg
Operating Profit 105.3 million stg
Information is a mix of print and electronic products in five main businesses.
(i) The Financial Times. Britain's leading business daily. Printed in some 10 centres worldwide, current circulation is around 300,000 -- 175,000 of which is in the UK.
(ii) FT Information. Supplier of electronic financial data and analysis for large institutional customers.
(iii) Les Echos Group. Publishes French business daily Les Echos and business monthly Enjeux.
(iv) Recoletos. Madrid-based. Titles include Spanish business newspaper Expansion and sports daily Marca. Pearson paid 87 million stg in August to boost stake by 30 percent to 95 percent.
(v) Pearson Professional. Supplies information and training materials to professionals in a range of industries.
The Information division agreed to sell its Westminster Press UK local newspaper operation to Newsquest for 305 million stg in August.
Pearson also has a 50 percent stake in the Economist Group, publishers of the Economist magazine.
EDUCATION:
Sales 358.9 million stg
Operating Profit 31.8 million stg
Pearson is a leading publisher of books for the U.S. and UK educational markets.
It acquired Harper Collins Educational Publishing Inc from News Corp for $580 million earlier at end-March 1996 and has merged it with its Addison Wesley Longman unit.
The acqusition made Pearson fourth in size among U.S. schoolbook publishers and third in the U.S. market for sales of college textbooks.
ENTERTAINMENT:
Sales 712.4 million stg
Operating Profit 110.9 million stg
Pearson's Entertainment interests embrace television, consumer publishing and visitor attractions.

Television. Pearson owns Thames Television, makers of some of Britain's favourites shows and Grundy Worldwide, producer of inexpensive drama series such as Australian soap "Neighbours". Pearson has a 24 percent stake in Britain's fifth terrestrial channel, which will launch next March. It also holds an indirect stake of some four percent in satellite broadscaster BSkyB.
Penguin Books. A world-famous imprint which has been in existence for over 60 years. Recently hired Michael Lynton, 36, a Walt Disney movie executive, as its new head.
Tussauds Group. Includes London's famous Madame Tussaud's waxworks and theme parks in Britain and Spain. Often seen as a prime candidate for disposal.

Mindscape. California-based consumer software unit that has been a tale of woe since its acquistion in a $462 million deal in 1994. Expected to lose around 46 million stg this year before returning to profit at the end of 1997.
Pearson New Entertainment. Produces videos, consumer magazines and CD-ROMS on subjects such as music and sport.
INVESTMENT BANKING:

Attributable profit 39.9 million stg. Consists mainly of Pearson's 50 percent stake in London merchant bank Lazards Brothers. Analyusts say there is little synergy with the core businesses and that the stake could be sold.
